original_question: Let X be the blow-up of P^2 at r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E be a (-1)-curve. For the restriction map rho : |D| -> |D|_E, is it true that (1) every base point in the image of rho comes from a base curve in |D|, and (2) if |D| has no fixed component, then rho has maximal rank?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 3.9.3 in Section 3.9, Imposing higher vanishing order at one point. The conjecture is set up by the exact restriction sequence comparing L(d; m1, ..., mn) with L(d; m1 + 1, m2, ..., mn), and it is followed by a separate, broader question for (-n)-curves in Problem 3.9.4. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft has already identified the correct target almost exactly: the right surface (the blow-up of P^2 at general points), the right quantified data (an effective divisor D and a (-1)-curve E), and the two precise conclusions stated in the paper: base points of the induced system on E should come from a base curve of |D|, and if |D| has no fixed component then the restriction map should have maximal rank. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places the conjecture inside the interpolation problem comparing L(d; m1, ..., mn) and L(d; m1 + 1, m2, ..., mn), using π:X→P^2, H=π^*L, exceptional divisors Ei=π^{-1}(pi), and D=dH-∑miEi; your draft omits this immediate setup. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

For full stand-alone precision, ρ should be defined as the linear restriction map on global sections H^0(X, OX(D)) → H^0(E, OE(D|E)); writing only ρ:|D|→|D|E leaves unclear what object is supposed to have rank. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The notation |D|E should be defined as the image linear system induced on E by restriction, not merely as an undefined restriction symbol. The text just before the conjecture explicitly says that the image of ρ is a linear system on E1. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

A paper-faithful formulation must keep the hypothesis that the blown-up points are general/generic; the authors immediately warn that the statement has counterexamples when points in special position are allowed. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The scope should remain exactly E a (-1)-curve. The paper treats the analogous question for (-n)-curves with n>1 only afterward, as a separate problem, so it should not be folded into the same question. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

To be self-contained, base curve should be clarified as a fixed curve component of the complete linear system |D| whose intersection with E produces a base point of the induced linear system on E; this is the phenomenon contrasted with no fixed component in part (2). ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

Section 3.9 does not impose any new base-field or characteristic hypothesis for this conjecture, so a faithful rewrite should avoid adding one that the paper does not state. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
refined_question: Let π:X→P^2 be the blow-up of r general points, let D be an effective divisor on X, and let E⊂X be a (-1)-curve. Let ρ:H^0(X, OX(D))→H^0(E, OE(D|E)) be the restriction map, and let |D|E⊂|OE(D|E)| denote its image linear system on E. Is it true that: (1) every base point of |D|E arises from a fixed curve component (base curve) of the complete linear system |D| meeting E; and (2) if |D| has no fixed component, then ρ has maximal rank? ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: Conjecture 3.9.3 states essentially these same two numbered assertions. The only substantive sharpening needed is to make the restriction map precise as the linear map on global sections coming from the exact sequence 0→OX(D−E1)→OX(D)→OE1(D|E1)→0, because maximal rank is naturally a property of that linear map, while |D|E is the induced image linear system on E. I also kept the scope exactly at general points and (-1)-curves, since the paper immediately notes counterexamples for points in special position and then moves to a separate Problem 3.9.4 for the (-n)-curve case. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
